references.text: Moses' prayer to God to see His glory ("Let me see your glory") is the direct precursor to Philip's request to see the Father, since Jesus later explains that seeing Him is seeing the Father.
Moses' prayer to know God's ways and find favor with Him parallels Philip's desire to know the Father in order to have enough, revealing a shared theme of seeking full insight into God's nature.
This text establishes that no one has ever seen God, but that the only Son has made Him known, which is the theological answer to Philip's question in 14:8.
Jesus states directly that whoever sees Him sees the One who sent Him, which provides the immediate context and response to Philip's claim that seeing the Father would be enough.
